title: Servant Leadership Is a Great Idea That Doesnt Really Work
author: Admired Leadership
summary: The author takes a contrarian stance on servant leadership, arguing that while the philosophy sounds appealing, it fails as a standalone operating model for most organizations. Servant leaders prioritize consensus, empathy, and putting others' needs first, but that emphasis can come at the expense of accountability, urgency, and strategic clarity. Without regular review of goals and clear expectations, teams under purely servant leadership drift, avoid hard feedback, and let responsibilities slip. The piece doesn't reject the underlying values of servant leadership, but insists they must be paired with discipline, candor, and results-orientation. The best leaders, in this view, blend servant instincts with firm accountability rather than choosing one over the other.
points: Servant leadership alone tends to under-deliver on accountability and strategic alignment.
Valuing consensus over urgency can slow decision-making and let opportunities slip.
Organizations led purely by servant leaders often suffer from 'mission creep.'
The philosophy is valuable for building trust but insufficient on its own for driving results.
The best leaders combine servant instincts with candid feedback and accountability.
quotes: With some notable workplace exceptions, servant leadership works better in theory than in practice.
The vast majority of enterprises, profit, and non-profit would implode under the guidance of a servant leader.
Servant leadership presumes others will operate in good faith and find the structure and support they need
Because servant leaders value consensus more than urgency and decisive action, opportunities are often lost
Examine an organization with a servant leader and you will likely see a lack of strategic alignment.
The best leaders are ALSO servant leaders. They support people while keeping their own ambitions and interests in check.
By putting the organization and the individual on equal footing, the best leaders are subservient in the right way.
